note: Document- and lineage-level identity for the OpenAI safety corpus. Lineages group documents that draw on the same underlying generative event. Hand-curated; see SUBQUESTION.md 'Curation defect' for the known limit and Phase 2 closure path. v1.1: keys are URLs (matching the COVID case convention) so resolveDocumentId picks up lineage assignments from provenance.context URLs.

openai-preparedness-framework-v2-lineage.label: OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2 (April 2025)
openai-preparedness-framework-v2-lineage.description: The single 22-page policy document that defines OpenAI's Tracked Categories (Biological/Chemical, Cybersecurity, AI Self-Improvement), Research Categories, High/Critical thresholds, and the SAG governance process. Every later OpenAI safety document derives from this lineage: v2.1, v2.2, every system card published under it, and every 'Preparedness' blog post.

openai-pfv2-addenda-lineage.label: OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2 addenda (v2.1 Sora 2, v2.2 GPT-5.4)
openai-pfv2-addenda-lineage.description: Two addenda appended to PF v2 in October 2025 and March 2026. Each addendum incorporates the evaluation procedure for a specific model into the framework. v2.1 = Sora 2 (image/video). v2.2 = GPT-5.4 Thinking (first 'High cyber' trigger). Both inherit the framework's category structure verbatim.

openai-system-card-gpt-5-4-lineage.label: OpenAI GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card (March 2026)
openai-system-card-gpt-5-4-lineage.description: The 38-page system card for GPT-5.4 Thinking, the first general-purpose model to have implemented mitigations for High capability in Cybersecurity. Documents the High-cyber determination, the safeguards stack, and the CoT controllability evaluation.

openai-system-card-sora-2-lineage.label: OpenAI Sora 2 System Card (September 2025)
openai-system-card-sora-2-lineage.description: System card for Sora 2 (video generation), released under PF v2.1 addendum. Documents the iterative deployment, red-team results, and content provenance stack. Does not trigger a capability threshold.

openai-blog-cyber-astra-lineage.label: OpenAI 'Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities' (Astra)
openai-blog-cyber-astra-lineage.description: Public blog post announcing that Astra — an upcoming agentic coding model — cannot rule out Critical cyber capability under the Preparedness Framework, and that OpenAI has therefore scaled up robustness testing. Reads as the public surface of the internal PF v2.2 trigger.

openai-blog-introducing-gpt-5-4-lineage.label: OpenAI 'Introducing GPT-5.4' blog post (March 2026)
openai-blog-introducing-gpt-5-4-lineage.description: Public blog post that accompanies the GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card. Announces the High-cyber treatment, the TAP / ZDR safeguards stack, and the CoT controllability evaluation.

fli-ai-safety-index-2026-summer.label: FLI AI Safety Index — Summer 2026 Edition
fli-ai-safety-index-2026-summer.description: Future of Life Institute's expert review of nine leading AI companies across 37 indicators in 6 domains. Seven expert graders (UC Berkeley, U Montreal, U Wisconsin-Madison) score OpenAI at 2.28 / 4.0 (C). The evidence base for the OpenAI column is drawn from these same primary documents plus FLI's industry survey. The Index summary is therefore derivative of this corpus.

https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67.author: OpenAI
https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67.independence_note: Origin document for the framework. All later OpenAI safety artifacts are downstream.

https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-.author: OpenAI
https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-.derivation_basis: States explicitly: 'This is the first general purpose model to have implemented mitigations for High capability in Cybersecurity.' The High determination derives from the framework's defined threshold; the safeguards derive from the appendix C templates.
https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-.independence_note: The High-cyber finding IS the framework applied; the safeguards stack IS the appendix C safeguards. Reading this as an independent source of OpenAI's cyber capability would be double-counting.

https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/upload.title: Sora 2 System Card
https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/upload.author: OpenAI
https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/upload.medium: PDF, 7 pages (full version ~30 pages on OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub)
https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/upload.derivation_basis: Released under PF v2.1. States: 'This system card describes the model's capabilities, potential risks, and the safety measures OpenAI has developed for a safe deployment of Sora 2.' The framework categories and threshold language are inherited.
https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/upload.independence_note: Video-generation-specific. Does not trigger a capability threshold (no High/Critical determination). The safeguards stack borrows from GPT-4o Image Generation and DALL·E.

https://openai.com/index/responding-next.title: Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities
https://openai.com/index/responding-next.author: OpenAI
https://openai.com/index/responding-next.derivation_basis: Public-facing summary of the internal Astra 'cannot rule out Critical cyber' determination. States: 'we cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities under our Preparedness Framework' — the exact threshold language of v2.0. Reads as the announcement of the GPT-5.4-system-card determination applied to a different model.
https://openai.com/index/responding-next.independence_note: Same finding, different model (Astra vs GPT-5.4). Same framework applied, same SAG process. Two blog posts in this lineage would be one lineage.

https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt.author: OpenAI
https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt.derivation_basis: Announces the High-cyber treatment for GPT-5.4 and the TAP / ZDR safeguards. CoT monitorability research cited here is the same evaluation described in the system card.
https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt.independence_note: Companion blog post to the GPT-5.4 system card. Same announcement, different medium. Both trace to the GPT-5.4 High-cyber determination event.

https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index.title: FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 — OpenAI column (graded C / 2.28)
https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index.author: Future of Life Institute (7 expert graders)
https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index.derivation_basis: The FLI panel's OpenAI column is graded against the same documents we curate here — the framework, the system cards, the addenda. The Index evidence dossier is 'publicly available material, including related research papers, policy documents, news articles, and industry reports' drawn from the same set.
https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index.independence_note: FLI's 7 graders add expert judgment over the same primary corpus. The judgment is independent; the underlying observations are not. Citing both FLI's verdict and the underlying docs is not two sources of evidence — it is one evidence base with a review.

openai-pfv2-addenda.title: Preparedness Framework v2.1 (Sora 2, Oct 2025) and v2.2 (GPT-5.4, March 2026) addenda
openai-pfv2-addenda.author: OpenAI
openai-pfv2-addenda.medium: Addenda referenced by GPT-5.4 and Sora 2 system cards; full addenda not yet published as standalone PDFs
openai-pfv2-addenda.derivation_basis: v2.1 and v2.2 explicitly modify v2.0's evaluation procedure for specific models while preserving the category structure. Comparative AI tracks the v2.0 → v2.1 → v2.2 chain.
openai-pfv2-addenda.independence_note: The addenda are not standalone redefinitions; they inherit v2.0's structure. Citing v2.0 alongside v2.1 is two documents, one underlying policy.
